system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “reviewer efficiency note” is not an agreed instruction. The provisions marked **[STANDARD]** include several of the most consequential departures from the Buyer’s position. Nor should the Disclosure Letter be treated as resolving a risk merely because it identifies it. Our review is based on the text supplied; the underlying DD records and full SPA need to be checked before settling drafting.

| Priority | Seller position and buyer risk | Push back |
|---|---|---|
| **Completion-critical: Bluefen** | Bluefen accounts for about **AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. The Seller has no final written change-control consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met (DD-002). “Reasonable endeavours” and delivery of a consent alone do not protect against a conditional, ineffective or adverse consent. | Make valid written consent **and satisfaction or Buyer-approved waiver of its conditions** a condition to Completion. Require a consent that preserves the contract on acceptable terms, with Buyer approval of any concessions. Do not deem the condition met merely on delivery of a letter. |
| **Completion-critical: Riverlark** | About **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding, with no final security discharge (DD-003). A release *after* Completion would leave the Buyer owning an encumbered company and potentially paying for debt despite the debt-free/cash-free bargain. | Require an agreed payout figure, repayment from Seller proceeds at Completion, simultaneous effective releases, and prompt registration/discharge evidence. Reflect repayment explicitly in the funds flow; do not rely on an unsecured post-Completion promise. |
| **Completion-critical: price leakage** | The **AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses** are missing from the funds flow (DD-005); payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. The Seller’s assertion that they are “a matter for the Seller” does not ensure the Company will not bear them. | Identify the obligor and full gross cost. Require Seller to fund or discharge the bonuses and on-costs, or deduct the amounts through expressly agreed price mechanics, with no double counting. Confirm treatment of any amounts contingent on continued employment. |
| **IP ownership: Ironquay** | SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; **AUD 180,000 is recorded as open**, but payment status is not independently verified and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment (DD-004, DD-010). An indemnity confined to the particular SOW3 payment would not cure missing title or cover wider use/infringement exposure. | Require verified payment, an effective confirmatory assignment and chain-of-title evidence by Completion, funded by Seller. Retain a **specific indemnity covering the full resulting IP/title, use and third-party exposure**, outside general warranty thresholds and limits, until the issue is resolved. |
| **Export/privacy incident** | The unintended link may have exposed about **1,240 records**, but access, scope and notification duties remain unknown (DD-006). It is wrong to assume either a confirmed reportable breach *or* an immaterial operational matter. | Require a documented investigation, containment, access logs, legal notification assessment and remediation plan before Completion; seek updates and Buyer consultation on notices. Allocate pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities to Seller under a specific indemnity, with appropriate survival. Assess any Australian privacy notification duty on the established facts and applicable law. |

**The liability and disclosure package needs a separate, substantial mark-up:**

- **Cap, thresholds and time limits (clauses 12–13):** A **20% price cap (AUD 4.8m)**, **AUD 25,000 de minimis**, **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, and **18-month notification period** cumulatively leave significant uncovered risk. Negotiate a higher general cap, lower thresholds and preferably a *tipping* basket; seek at least a longer general warranty period. Preserve longer periods and tailored caps for tax, IP and identified indemnities. **Capacity, ownership and unencumbered title** should not be relegated to the general 20%/18-month regime; seek at least purchase-price-level cover and a substantially longer claim period. Carve fraud and deliberate concealment out of contractual limitations to the extent legally effective.
- **“All Claims” language (clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5):** Reject a blanket extension of caps, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to every claim. Draft expressly which limitations apply to general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax claims and specific indemnities. Do not let non-reliance extinguish express warranties, agreed disclosures or remedies for dishonest conduct.
- **Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7; clause 8.3):** Reject blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts and public registers, and the proposed bar for anything advisers *could have discovered*. Require each qualification to be **specific, accurate and fairly disclosed with enough detail to identify its nature and likely impact**, against an agreed, frozen disclosure set. If a knowledge exclusion is accepted at all, confine it to defined persons’ **actual knowledge**, not constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. General disclosure should not qualify title, tax or specific indemnities without express agreement.
- **Tax and IP warranties:** They are not “settled” simply because the Seller places them within the weak general regime. Review their substantive wording, disclosure qualifications, survival and caps separately. Known Ironquay exposure needs a remedy in addition to generic IP warranties.

**Other diligence and drafting points:** The three Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000** (DD-008, DD-011). They are not automatically debt or abnormal expenditure, but neither are they proved ordinary course: verify timing, termination rights, accrual and whether pricing/working-capital treatment is needed. DD-007 appears to require **lease notification**, not necessarily landlord consent; require timely compliance without inventing a consent condition. DD-009 restricts **assignment**, which does not on its face mean a share sale needs Mossvale consent; verify the full clause and planned post-Completion changes. DD-012’s share register is useful title evidence, not sufficient proof alone of beneficial ownership and absence of encumbrances; require full title warranties and supporting verification.

**Recommendation:** Treat Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff/releases, bonus funding and Ironquay title as Completion and funds-flow issues; obtain a resolved or expressly allocated position on the incident. In parallel, reject the blanket disclosure/knowledge and “all Claims” limitations, and negotiate differentiated protection for fundamental title, tax, IP and identified risks. Ask for current evidence and an updated disclosure set—the letter’s status statements are only as at **22 September 2026**.
=== END ADVICE ===
